escalation.calibration_first: Calibration before router cleverness: a well-calibrated 70% that knows it is 70% routes better than an overconfident 95% wrong 30% of the time.
escalation.retraction: Interpretations MUST be retractable; ASP-style defaults with named exceptions; Dung argument graph as the audit of which interpretation attacked which and survived.
escalation.routing_table: Confidence x cost alone misroutes; the routing table must carry, per channel, latency, reversibility, and channel-specific false-positive cost, on top of functional routing.
escalation.rule: Posterior over states, utility matrix over actions (act / wait / escalate / ask another channel), value-of-information for each additional channel or second of recording; escalate only when value-of-information > cost; a threshold is the point where expected loss from acting equals expected loss from waiting plus the cost of the next observation.
escalation.scope_note: The JEV lean rule (null OR confidence < 0.8) is a code-task rule; it is NOT transplanted to routing decisions by this index. Routing escalation is the value-of-information rule above.
escalation.tiers: Tiers calibrated to action cost (log < notify < intervene < actuate irreversibly), confidence MARGIN (not just top score) as the routing variable, and a budget on how often the top tier may fire.

escalation.multidimensional: A multidimensional shape is the joint object of per-dimension shapes K_d under gluing constraints G; without G there is a collection of shapes, not a multidimensional one. Failure mode: gluing blindness (every per-dimension shape fine while joint structure stays invisible from every single dimension).
escalation.order: Difference imaging first, in order: (1) reconstruct CHANGES from a baseline; (2) choose the prior deliberately and name it; (3) compute and publish the Jacobian singular-value spectrum and state, in cm, what cannot be seen; (4) report uncertainty as a map, not a single image.
escalation.prebuild_decision: Linear vs nonlinear shaves must be decided before any shaving build: half-space intersection always yields convex sets, erosion preserves concavity; address patterns have holes/gaps, so linear shaves recover only the convex shadow. No shaving build was ordered.
escalation.reporting: Report the SET of states consistent with the data, with regularisation stated, not a single reconstructed shape presented as fact.
escalation.rule: Commit to a band only when the whole bracket lies inside it; escalate (measure more, wait, raise resolution) when the bracket straddles a band boundary.

task_kind_tagging.guide: A task declares its kind with a single field: {"task_kind": "<one of the modes keys>"}. The dispatcher looks up modes[task_kind] and applies that mode's seats, escalation, tests, avoid list, and cost posture, citing the mode's sources. The tag is declared by the task author (e.g. a goal task); the dispatcher does not infer it.
task_kind_tagging.unknown_kind: If task_kind is missing or not one of the modes keys, no mode applies. Do not default to another kind's rules and do not invent a mode; record the task as untagged and leave seat/escalation selection to an explicit order.
task_kind_tagging.unresolved_fields: A mode field whose value is the string starting with 'unresolved' means the map states no grounded rule or seat for that field. Do not fill it in from another kind or from outside the map; treat it as an open design question for perg.
